beats: Hook (p15, 40:43-42:29): every extra wire on a chip saves SWAP gates, so which layout is better? The denser one, obviously. So why did IBM's newer chips give each qubit fewer neighbours, not more? (line_qc_chip_wires_refused). Cast as in QC03-01: the fabricator = the chip maker, the planner = the compiler; new prop: a tuning fork = one qubit, its pitch = the qubit's frequency. p15's smiley faces are clip art: cover them.
Dense saves SWAPs (55:31-57:07): a two-qubit gate between qubits that are not linked costs SWAPs, and a 10-CNOT program can triple (reuse line_qc_pass_seat_swap).
The trend (tape p16, 42:42-44:55): IBM went sparse, dense, then sparse again (heavy-hex: at most three neighbours); Google keeps a square grid with four. Check the IBM topology history in FACTS.md.
Each qubit is driven by microwave pulses at its own frequency, set when the chip is made; she calls the frequency the fingerprint of each qubit (clip 53:45-54:13).

Too similar = crosstalk (46:14-47:52): a pulse meant for one qubit also drives a linked neighbour with the same frequency, like a second tuning fork humming along (line_qc_chip_forks_same; sympathetic resonance is a real effect, so the picture is honest).

Too different = slow two-qubit gates (48:26-49:00): (line_qc_chip_forks_far). So linked neighbours must differ, but not by much: a careful frequency plan for the whole chip (line_qc_chip_forks_board).

Fabrication spread (50:10-51:04): you plan 12, you get 15; with more links, more linked pairs can collide, and a collision can make the chip useless; the final thing is fabrication yield (clip 45:47-46:14) (line_qc_chip_forks_batch, then line_qc_chip_reject_bin). The yield plots on p17-p18 are third-party (Brink et al. 2018; Hertzberg et al. 2021): redraw as a falling line, never tape them.

General-purpose vs application-specific (tape p19, 57:48-59:07; clip 58:13-58:40): dense links only where the target program needs them; "one good chip in 500" is her illustration, never captioned as data.

The design flow (tape p20, 59:20-60:39; Li, Ding, Xie, ASPLOS 2020): profile the program, add links only as needed (line_qc_chip_desire_paths: pave only the paths people actually walk). Honest limit: a chip shaped for one program serves other programs less well.
Research advice (clip 51:29-52:22): find the physical limitation, or improve a known solution (reuse line_mic).

Cover (line_qc_cover_03_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the planner offers an armful of wires, the fabricator folds his arms beside a sparse honeycomb tile and a bin of dense rejects.
